content.jointProblem: What mechanisms cause fatigue cracking at AutomVoj’s painted mild-steel conveyor welds in 2–6 °C cold stores, and could changes to welding procedure, filler material or joint geometry reduce damage under representative service conditions? The first experiment would compare production-representative joints under measured service loading at room temperature and under service-matched chilled and condensation conditions, using examination of the recovered failures to test whether laboratory damage reproduces the field mechanism before evaluating modifications.

rationale.text: Erić has directly relevant experimental experience investigating the interaction of mechanical fatigue and thermal cycling in welded structural steel.

sources.quote: Four loading programmes were applied: isothermal fatigue at 20 °C, isothermal fatigue at −30 °C, in-phase thermo-mechanical fatigue (TMF), and out-of-phase TMF

rationale.text: He has experience translating field strain and temperature measurements into fatigue assessments, which is relevant to replacing the company's room-temperature-only loading assumptions with service evidence.

sources.quote: Rainflow-counted stress spectra and simultaneous temperature records were used to construct a combined loading environment for assessment.

rationale.text: His work combines measured weld residual stresses with thermal–mechanical simulation, providing a basis for investigating welding-related contributors rather than assuming temperature alone causes the failures.

sources.quote: were measured by hole-drilling with strain-gauge rosettes and compared with sequentially coupled thermal–mechanical FE simulations.

rationale.text: His group routinely uses fatigue-testing, climate-chamber and finite-element tools relevant to a controlled investigation of the company's failure mechanism.

sources.quote: The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C, and in-house FE models built in Abaqus

rationale.text: A joint project matches his explicitly stated interest in low-temperature and combined-loading fatigue testing collaborations.

sources.quote: joint projects involving fatigue testing under low-temperature or combined loading conditions

constraints.text: Testing must represent the actual mild-steel hollow-section connections and 2–6 °C service environment; room-temperature load tests alone cannot establish that the field mechanism has been reproduced.

sources.quote: Our conveyor frames are welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery.
We test frames under load at room temperature and they pass without any problem.

constraints.text: The investigation needs access to the existing failure evidence and a sampling plan that preserves enough of the two recovered sections for complementary examinations.

sources.quote: We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage.

constraints.text: A laboratory route for simultaneous chilled cyclic loading must be arranged outside the company's current capabilities; suitable fixtures and environmental control must be confirmed before committing to the campaign.

sources.quote: We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load.
The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C

constraints.text: Extended testing must be scheduled in advance because the researcher's climate chamber and fatigue machine are shared resources.

sources.quote: Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

constraints.text: The company must allocate named engineering support around live project commitments; a plan cannot assume a dedicated internal R&D team.

sources.quote: We have no dedicated R&D department
our chief engineer and two senior automation engineers who allocate time between live projects and improvement work.

constraints.text: The investigation must connect the proposed failure mechanism to testable manufacturing or design changes, rather than ending with a generic fatigue-life calculation.

sources.quote: understanding exactly what is causing the cracks so we can change our welding procedure, filler material, or joint design

risks: Transfer is unvalidated: the cited thermal-fatigue studies use different steel grades, joint geometries and substantially colder temperature cycles. Their mechanisms and numerical improvements cannot be assumed for painted hollow sections at 2–6 °C; the first comparative experiment must test this transfer.

Condensation or corrosion-assisted fatigue could matter, but the supplied research evidence does not establish expertise or equipment for controlled condensation testing of painted welds. Additional capability or a specialist partner may be needed.

Service load spectra, thermal histories, humidity and coating condition are unknown. An accelerated test could reproduce cracking through a different mechanism and lead to an ineffective modification.
Only two failed sections are reported available; destructive sampling could exhaust evidence before competing failure explanations are assessed.

The researcher's personal availability, confirmed equipment slots, company budget and required completion date remain unknown. Shared equipment and limited company engineering capacity could delay the work.
questions: Can Erić confirm his availability, proposed team and earliest access to the shared fatigue machine and climate chamber?
Can the laboratory accommodate representative hollow-section joints under cyclic loading at 2–6 °C while controlling humidity or condensation, or is external equipment needed?
Can AutomVoj provide drawings, exact steel grades and wall thicknesses, welding procedures, filler specifications, inspection records and coating details for failed and unaffected frames?
Can customer sites support strain or vibration, temperature and humidity monitoring, including belt loading, starts and stops, washdowns and any defrost cycles?
What examination and destructive-sampling permissions apply to the two failed sections, and are matched unfailed sections or new production specimens available?
What budget, decision deadline and company engineering time are available, and who will own site access, specimen fabrication and implementation trials?
What evidence will be required to accept a proposed change, including agreement on mechanism matching, comparative fatigue testing and subsequent field monitoring?
